text: After this you can design a basic identification and revision scheme.

An identifier lets someone distinguish one item or version from another. Product types, individual units, documents and revisions can need different codes. A part number often names a design, while a serial number identifies one physical example. A software release identifier distinguishes builds. Whatever symbols a team chooses, the rule for assigning and changing them should be consistent and documented.

items: Decide whether the record names a design, a unit, a file or a release. You should see: The identifier has a clear purpose. If not: Avoid one field that mixes all four.
Choose a readable, nonrepeating scheme. You should see: People can tell items apart without guessing. If not: Check existing identifiers before issuing a new one.
Link markings and records where practical. You should see: The inspected item can be matched to its entry. If not: Record any unreadable or lost marking.
Control identifier changes and supersessions. You should see: A prior code still leads to its successor. If not: Keep an alias or history rather than silently overwriting.
Inferred: Module-02 identifies a design. Unit-0057 identifies an individual item. Software-2.3 identifies a program version. Their jobs should not be confused.

text: Give each identifier one clear meaning and a stable history.
A marking system alone cannot show authorization or installed status.

items: Using the same code for a design and an individual unit Records cannot distinguish the type from its instances. Fix: Separate design, serial and revision fields.
